stem:
Mehak reads that Earth takes nearly 365.25 days to revolve around the Sun. Her wall calendar uses 365 days most years and adds one extra day every fourth year.

Which statements correctly explain why that leap day is needed?

statements.text: The extra quarter-days add up to about one full day every four years.
Adding that leap day keeps the solar calendar aligned with the seasons.
The leap day is added so the calendar matches the Moon's phases each month.

teacher.key_rationale: Earth's nearly 365.25-day revolution leaves quarter-days that sum to about one day every four years; a leap day keeps seasons aligned. Linking the leap day to Moon phases confuses solar and lunar calendars.
